what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1960?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1960 annual town report (120 pages) prints no wage list: the whole text was searched for wages, payroll, gross, salary and employ and found only the `Wages` object lines inside the accountant's schedule (p26-36, by department, not by person), prose about payroll deductions (p74, p118) and the individual salaries of elected officers as voted lines (p58-59 budget; Selectmen's, Assessors', Treasurer's, Tax Collector's and Town Clerk's salaries) — closes: a payroll register or the Treasurer's warrants for calendar 1960

what: What were the town's salary grades and step rates in 1960?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1960 report was searched for `salary schedule` (the only hit is a quoted National Education Association statement on p118, no schedule) and for any grade or step table (none on the 120 pages; teachers are listed by name, education and years only, p108-112) — closes: the town's 1960 wage and salary by-law, and the School Committee's salary schedule

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1960, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1960 report prints no such schedule: `revolving` appears nowhere in the text; the balance sheet (p16-17) shows federal grants ($12,516.64) and unexpended balances ($150,802.34) as liabilities, and the school lunch (p117) and athletic (p118) accounts are the School Department's own statements — closes: the Treasurer's or Accountant's fund-by-fund ledger for 1960

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in 1960?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1960 report prints no such schedule: the capital projects are special articles in the accountant's schedule (p31, p35: Jr.-Sr. High School Addition, Chapter 90 construction) and the borrowing is in the text of p63 (Special Town Meeting, August 18, 1960: $327,500 and $17,500; $227,500 bonds authorized, unissued, on the p16-17 balance sheet) — closes: a project-by-project capital ledger

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1960?
why: `report-valuation` holds the valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1960 report gives the assessed valuation as real estate $9,272,790 and personal property $436,820 (p6 text; p9 table) and the tax rate $71.50 (p6, p9), with no levy, overlay-by-year or new-growth table: `overlay` is searched on p17, p37 and p59 and appears only as the balance-sheet reserve (Overlays Reserved for Abatements, Tax Levy of 1960, $7,088.35) and the Overlay Surplus transfer — closes: the Assessors' tax recapitulation for 1960

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1960, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and `sealing-fee-schedule` the fee per device from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1960 report gives the year's total in prose (p43: one hundred sixty-seven devices adjusted and sealed) and the fees collected as one receipt line (p21: Sealer's Fees $94.60); no count or fee by type of device (searched p5, 21, 22, 29, 43, 59, 119) — closes: the Sealer's annual return to the Division of Standards

what: How did each trust fund move in 1960: opening balance, interest and bequests received, and closing balance?
why: `report-trust-funds` holds fund roll-forwards from the 1981 report. The 1960 report prints the year-end balances by fund and donor (p17, $68,384.06) and the receipts and deposits of 1960 as payment and receipt lines (p20 and p24: bequests $800.00, income by fund); there is no Trust Fund Commission report in the text (`trust fund` appears on p4, 20, 24, 37, 58, 119 only) — closes: the Trust Fund Commissioners' 1960 report
